G.D. Goenka School, Darbhanga · Term I Notebook Validation 2026-27

Notebook Validation Drive — what the validators reported contains student names — school record

Every validation e-mail received between 29 July and 3 August was re-read with no keyword filter, every photographed sheet rendered and read, and every mark interpreted against the plan of 74 class-subject validations. This is what those reports say, what they leave unsaid, and where notebooks are still unchecked.

Audited 4 August 2026, 01:00 IST898 mailbox messages re-read with no keyword filter; 50 validation reports; 91 attachments; 140 rendered sheet pages read; roster pulled fresh from the ERP 861 students · 27 sections · 6,637 planned checks

The one thing to take from this audit: a tick tells you a notebook was produced. It does not tell you the subject teacher had checked it, whether the work was up to date, or when a teacher last saw it. That gap is why Director Ma'am wrote on 29 July, “the validation is not solving our purpose”, and why Office Order GDGPSD/2026-27/OFFICE/042 was issued on 30 July adding Last checked on (date) / unchecked and Complete / Incomplete columns. Reports written before that date cannot answer those questions retrospectively. Under her instruction of 30 July, “Incomplete and not aligned with the requirements to be considered as NOT SUBMITTED.”

What the marks on the sheets mean

Reading a sheet correctly depends on this vocabulary — and on treating an empty box as a real signal rather than a pass.

✓ / CompleteNotebook produced and accepted by the validator. Does NOT certify that the subject teacher had checked it.
NS / Not Submitted / Not BroughtStudent produced no notebook. Written NS (AB) when the cause was absence, NS (Not Brought) when the child was present.
AB / AbsentStudent absent that day. Legitimate — but the notebook is still unchecked and must be re-run.
NC / T.N.C. / Not CheckedTEACHER LAPSE. The work was done; the subject teacher never checked or signed it.
INC / Incomplete / W.I.C.Student lapse — work not up to date, pages or exercises missing.
N.M. — Index not madeIndex page never started. N.C. on Mr. Abhaydeep's sheets means 'index not completed'.
Index / Date / P.G. missingMaintenance defects recorded in the Remarks column.
Left / New / TransferredStudent has left, joined recently, or moved section. Roster correction, not a defect.
(blank)NO VERDICT RECORDED. Treat as NOT VALIDATED — a blank block of rows means those notebooks never reached the validator.

Corrections to the first-pass check

This audit re-read the whole mailbox with no keyword filter. Three findings from the earlier internal check were wrong and are corrected here.

correctedFour more reports arrived late on the night of 3 August, after the first version of this page went up

Mr. Farhan sent Class III Information Technology at 21:38. Mr. Diwas Rai sent Class VIII Hindi at 21:59 — his first report of the entire drive, having been covered by Ms. Chhumi and Ms. Avni since 29 July. Ms. Avni sent Class VIII English AND Social Science at 23:36 in a single mail titled only 'Social Science'. Coverage moved from 45 to 49 of the 62 validations due by Monday, and Class VIII from 3 of 8 to 6 of 8.

correctedA counting error on this page has been corrected

Class III was shown as 4 of 4 when it was 3 of 4. English had been validated ahead of its 4 August date, and that early completion was wrongly allowed to fill the gap left by Information Technology, which was then still missing. The headline read 46 when it should have read 45. Information Technology has since arrived, so Class III is now genuinely 4 of 4 — but the figure was wrong for a day. Every counter on this page is now computed from the schedule rather than entered by hand, so the same mistake cannot recur.

correctedClass III was never a blackout

Mr. Syed Farhan Ahmad reported on 29 July with five scanned sheets — Mathematics, Hindi Literature, Hindi Grammar, General Knowledge and English — again on 31 July for GK III-B, and again on 3 August for Information Technology. An earlier internal check missed these because the mailbox search used the word 'valid', which does not match 'Validation' in Gmail.

correctedClass VI is fully covered

Ms. Ankita Kerketta sent three further reports late on 31 July and Mr. Abhaydeep Kumar sent English and Sanskrit/Urdu on 3 August. All eight validations due are in. The problem in Class VI is not coverage — it is what the sheets show.

correctedClass X Physics was delivered, not missed

Mr. Santu could not run it on 1 August because Mr. Satyananda was absent, obtained a written commitment, and the signed sheet arrived on 3 August along with Class X Information Technology.

correctedThe roster has moved since the drive was planned

The plan was built on 859 students; the ERP pull returns 861 active students in Classes I–X across the same 27 sections. The class charts use the fresh ERP roster.

Class-by-class chart — every student, every subject

Pulled fresh from the ERP on 3 August: 861 active students across 27 sections. Every subject the drive scheduled for that class is a column. Read across a row to see one child's whole term; read down a column to see one subject. The flag count sorts the worst cases to the top.

Problems with the reports themselves

Separate from what the notebooks showed: how the reporting was done.

ProblemWhereWhy it matters
Covering mail contradicts the sheet attached to itClass VIII Social Science (1 Aug) and Class III Information Technology (3 Aug)Ms. Avni's mail states 'All notebooks have been checked and validated as per the prescribed guidelines' while her own sheet shows roughly half of VIII A as NS and three students marked 'Not checked'. Mr. Farhan's mail says '53 validated, 3 absent' where his sheet says 52 validated, 3 not produced, 1 absent. Read the sheet, not the mail.
A report submitted as a spreadsheet whose own totals disagreeClass VIII Hindi, Mr. Diwas, 3 AugThe dashboard tab says 116 notebooks and 7 absent; the class-wise table directly beneath says 125 and 16. The tab titled 'All 125 Students Record' holds about 46 rows. One entry reads 'Not Submitted note erased'. The 16 named defaulters are usable; the totals are not.
Reports sent late, in batchesClass IV (four reports batched on 1 Aug), Class VI (all six of Ms. Ankita's 1–3 days late), Class VII (30 Jul sheets sent 1 Aug), Class IX Biology and EnglishThe Office Order requires the signed sheet to be photographed and mailed the SAME DAY. A batch arriving three days later, out of order, with no class or subject in the subject line, is what prompted 'I am not able to understand the report.'
Defaulter Summary box left emptyClass II GK, IT and Science; Class IX Sanskrit; Class X Social Science; Class VI GK (one line only)Counts without names make follow-up impossible. That box exists so the defaulter list is produced during the drive rather than reconstructed afterwards — the single biggest fix made after PT-1.
Summary counts not filled at allClass VI Financial Literacy, Mathematics and Information TechnologyThe named defaulters are there, but with no totals the sheet cannot be reconciled against the roster.
Sheet never photographedClass X Chemistry and Mathematics (mail body only); Class III GK for III-B (list handed to Ms. Prerna before it could be photographed)No signed, certified sheet on file means nothing can be audited or shown to management. Mr. Farhan flagged this himself and offered to submit photographs later — take him up on it.
Blank rows treated as doneClass II Maths (11 rows), Class V Hindi (all of V B), Class V Science (60 students), Class X Hindi (three sections), Class IV Hindi (IV A, IV B), Class IX English (IX A, IX B), Class IX Sanskrit (100 students)A blank box is not a pass. Where a block of rows is blank, those notebooks were never seen, and the summary line should say so.
Two validators on one class, unannouncedClass VI — Mr. Abhaydeep Kumar (assigned) and Ms. Ankita Kerketta both reported, in parallel, with no handover noteCoverage happened to come out complete, but nobody knew who to chase, and Mr. Abhaydeep reported from a personal address rather than his school ID.
Substitutions not recordedClass VIII — Mr. Diwas → Ms. Chhumi Hang Rai → Ms. Avni Kaushik. One sheet signed 'for' another personSubstitution is fine when a validator is away on CBSE cluster or other duty; an unannounced substitution means the certification signature no longer matches the assigned validator.
Mail routingClass VIII Financial Literacy reminder addressed to Director Ma'am rather than to Mr. ArkoDirector Ma'am's correction today: the mail should go to the teacher, keeping the coordinator and her in CC — the same rule as the drive mails themselves.
Validator shorthand that cannot be matched to a child11 names written on sheets or in typed tables — 1 in Class I, 1 in Class IV, 9 in Class VIValidators wrote a first name only or a spelling the ERP roster does not carry (e.g. 'Sammar', 'Namansh', 'Matifar', 'Jabhyata', 'Nayan Kr. Jha'). These findings are real but cannot be attached to a specific student, so they appear in the student list and not in the class charts. Full name as per the ERP, please.

This page names individual students and admission numbers, published on the instruction of the Academic Coordinator so that every teacher, validator and member of management can see the same record. It is excluded from search-engine indexing. Please treat it as a school document and do not circulate it outside the school community.

Sources: the full mailbox for 28 July – 3 August 2026 (898 mailbox messages re-read with no keyword filter; 50 validation reports; 91 attachments; 140 rendered sheet pages read; roster pulled fresh from the ERP), read message by message with no keyword filter. Counts are transcribed from the handwritten Defaulter Summary boxes and Remarks columns; where a validator left a box blank, that is recorded as blank rather than inferred. Plan of record: Term I Notebook Validation 2026-27, 74 subject-dates across 27 sections.
